chunks: Is'haq ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying:
I was with my father one day, and 'Ali ibn 'Umar ibn 'Ali asked him, saying: “May I be sacrificed for you, to whom shall we turn, and to whom shall the people turn, after you?”

So he said: “To the owner of the two yellow garments and the two locks of hair”—meaning the two braids—“and he is the one who will appear before you from this door, opening the two doors together with his hand.”
Then we did not remain long before two hands appeared to us, taking hold of the two doors and opening them. Then Abū Ibrāhīm entered upon us.

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the Kunyah of Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام
key_terms.الذُّؤَابَتَيْنِ: the two braids or tresses, clarifying the previous description
key_terms.الْغَدِيرَتَيْنِ: the two hanging locks or braided strands of hair
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الثَّوْبَيْنِ الْأَصْفَرَيْنِ: the man identified by wearing two yellow garments
key_terms.نَفْزَعُ: we turn in distress or seek recourse

ai.seo_question: Whom did the Imam عليه السلام identify as the religious authority after him?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an indication by an Imam عليه السلام toward Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام as the one to whom people should turn after him. The report presents a clear identifying description followed by the immediate appearance of the designated successor, highlighting religious authority within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary who said,

‘Is’haq son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> narrated to me saying, ‘I was in the presence of my father<sup>asws</sup> one day, so Ali Bin Umar Bin Ali asked him<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! To who should we turn to (when in distress), and the people in desperate need, after you<sup>asws</sup>?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘To the owner of the two yellow clothes, and the two streams, meaning the two tresses (of hair), and he<sup>asws</sup> would be emerging to you from this door’. He<sup>asws</sup> opened the two doors together.
So we did not wait long before there emerged to us two palms grabbing the two doors, and opened them. Then Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) entered coming towards us’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ya‘qub ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari who has said that Ishaq ibn Ja‘far (a.s.) said to me the following.

“One day I was in the presence of my father that Ali ibn ‘Umar ibn Ali asked him this question. “‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, “from who should we seek help and the people seek help and assistance after you (leave this world)?”

He (The Imam (a.s.) said, you must seek refuge and guidance from the man who has two yellow clothes on him and a twine bunch of hair who will shortly appear to you from this door, opening the both halves of the door with his hand together.”
We did not wait very long that there appeared two palms holding both halves of the door and opened them. Thereafter came to us abu Ibrahim (a.s.).”
